'''Jens Beckmann''' (born 1970) is a German-Australian scientist working as professor in the area of synthetic [[Inorganic chemistry|inorganic]] and [[organometallic chemistry]] at the [[University of Bremen]] since 2010. Previously he worked as assistant professor at the [[Free University of Berlin]] (2004–2010) and as lecturer at [[Deakin University]] in [[Geelong]] (2002–2004). He is best known for the preparation of reactive and functional molecules including the first stable [[nitrene]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal |last1=Janssen |first1=Marvin |last2=Frederichs |first2=Thomas |last3=Olaru |first3=Marian |last4=Lork |first4=Enno |last5=Hupf |first5=Emanuel |last6=Beckmann |first6=Jens |date=2024-07-19 |title=Synthesis of a stable crystalline nitrene |journal=Science |volume=385 |issue=6706 |pages=318–321 |doi=10.1126/science.adp4963 |issn=1095-9203 |pmid=38870274|bibcode=2024Sci...385..318J }}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Beckmann was born in December 1970 in [[Arnsberg]], [[Westphalia]], [[Germany]], and grew up in the near village of Oeventrop. He graduated from the Gymnasium Laurentianum Arnsberg obtaining his Abitur in 1990. He studied [[Chemistry]] at the [[Technical University of Dortmund|University of Dortmund]], where he obtained his Diploma in 1995 and his Ph.D. ("Dr. rer nat.") in 1999 under the supervision of Prof Klaus Jurkschat. Starting in early 2000, he worked for two years as Feodor Lynen fellow of the [[Alexander von Humboldt Foundation|Alexander von Humboldt foundation]] at [[Deakin University|Deakin University Geelong]] under the guidance of Prof Dainis Dakternieks.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Prof. Dr. Jens Beckmann |url=https://www.humboldt-foundation.de/en/connect/explore-the-humboldt-network/singleview/1067747/prof-dr-jens-beckmann |access-date=2024-08-22 |website=www.humboldt-foundation.de |language=en}}</ref>

== Career ==
Beckmann's first independent facility position was at the Centre for Chiral and Molecular Technologies at [[Deakin University|Deakin]]. With his small research group, he investigated functional organotin and organotellurium compounds including polymeric telluroxanes and bimetallic systems capable of absorbing [[carbon dioxide]] from [[air]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Beckmann |first1=Jens |last2=Dakternieks |first2=Dainis |last3=Duthie |first3=Andrew |last4=Lewcenko |first4=Naomi A. |last5=Mitchell |first5=Cassandra |date=2004-12-10 |title=Carbon Dioxide Fixation by the Cooperative Effect of Organotin and Organotellurium Oxides |url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/anie.200460155 |journal=Angewandte Chemie International Edition |volume=43 |issue=48 |pages=6683–6685 |doi=10.1002/anie.200460155 |pmid=15593160 |issn=1433-7851|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

Besides his academic work, he was involved in the commercial research activities of the spin-off company ''Chirogen Pty Ltd'' in 2002 to 2004, developing enantioselective reducing agents.

At the Institute for Chemistry and Biochemistry, he continued working as an assistant professor from 2004 to 2010 with his group on heavy ''p''-block element compounds, which included (mixed valent) [[tellurium]] [[halide]]s,<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Beckmann |first1=Jens |last2=Hesse |first2=Malte |last3=Poleschner |first3=Helmut |last4=Seppelt |first4=Konrad |date=2007 |title=Formation of mixed-valent aryltellurenyl halides RX2TeTeR |journal=Angewandte Chemie International Edition in English |volume=46 |issue=43 |pages=8277–8280 |doi=10.1002/anie.200702341 |issn=1521-3773 |pmid=17876865}}</ref> and well-defined tellurinic, telluronic and stibonic [[acid]]s.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Beckmann |first1=Jens |last2=Finke |first2=Pamela |last3=Hesse |first3=Malte |last4=Wettig |first4=Burkhard |date=2008-12-08 |title=Well-Defined Stibonic and Tellurinic Acids |url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/anie.200803997 |journal=Angewandte Chemie International Edition |volume=47 |issue=51 |pages=9982–9984 |doi=10.1002/anie.200803997 |pmid=19006136 |issn=1433-7851|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Beckmann |first1=Jens |last2=Bolsinger |first2=Jens |last3=Finke |first3=Pamela |last4=Hesse |first4=Malte |date=2010-10-18 |title=A Well-Defined Dinuclear Telluronic Acid [RTe(μ-O)(OH) 3 ] 2 |url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/anie.201002545 |journal=Angewandte Chemie International Edition |volume=49 |issue=43 |pages=8030–8032 |doi=10.1002/anie.201002545 |pmid=20839196 |issn=1433-7851|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

Since 2010, he has been an associate professor at the University of Bremen. At the Faculty for Biology and Chemistry, Beckmann co-founded the Institute for [[Inorganic chemistry|Inorganic Chemistry]] and [[Crystallography]] in 2015. == Awards and honors ==

* Rudolf Chaudoire-Award of the [[Technical University of Dortmund|University of Dortmund]] for the best Ph.D. thesis in 1999.

* Feodor Lynen Scholarship of the [[Alexander von Humboldt Foundation|Alexander von Humboldt-Foundation]]<ref name=":1" />

* Doctor honoris causa from the N. N. Vorozhtsov Novosibrisk Institute of Organic Chemistry of the [[Russian Academy of Sciences|Russian Academy of Science]], Siberian Branch.

== Books & publications ==
He is the author of more than 270 peer-reviewed publications,<ref>{{Cite web |title=ORCID |url=https://orcid.org/0000-0002-8548-1821 |access-date=2024-08-19 |website=orcid.org}}</ref> 9 book chapters and 16 patent applications.
